road.title: Please, thank you, sorry
road.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard under a hat that has seen service, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Leopold is a Fast Talker and was cursed to speak at twice the usual speed and has made peace with being asked to slow down.

openObjectives.prompt: Leopold has something you need and a firm view of how it should be asked for. Ask Leopold for something and say please, using Italian.
Leopold is busy with something that matters only to Leopold. Get Leopold's attention politely, using Italian.
Leopold has just said something long, fast and apparently urgent. Tell Leopold that you do not understand, using Italian.

character.name: Leopold Wimple
character.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard under a hat that has seen service, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Leopold is a Fast Talker and was cursed to speak at twice the usual speed and has made peace with being asked to slow down.

npc.narrative: You reach the bosco on a clear mattina, the cielo wide open and entirely unfiled. Leopold Wimple waits at a small tavolo with a timbro in one hand and a blank foglio in the other, looking like a man whose strada to promotion ended at the first corner.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Scusi, parlo molto veloce. Non capisco il silenzio. Per favore, come ti chiami?
npc.translation: Good morning! Excuse me, I speak very fast. I don't understand silence. Please, what is your name?

player: Buongiorno! Mi chiamo Marco. Scusi, non capisco... silenzio?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You greeted Leopold, told him your name, and politely said you didn't understand the word \"silenzio\".

objectiveResults.feedback: You didn't ask for anything with the Italian word for "please" this time; try asking Leopold for something and add it. It will come up again later.
Well done, you used "Scusi" politely to get Leopold's attention.
Great, "non capisco" is exactly right for saying you don't understand.

openObjectives.prompt: Leopold has something you need and a firm view of how it should be asked for. Ask Leopold for something and say please, using Italian.
Leopold is busy with something that matters only to Leopold. Get Leopold's attention politely, using Italian.
Leopold has just said something long, fast and apparently urgent. Tell Leopold that you do not understand, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Leopold sets down his penna and regards you, il capo of a very small department. On the tavolo a rubber stamp waits, unused, beside a caffè gone cold. The mattina is clear, and nobody has filled in the pause.
npc.native: Piacere, Marco! Un momento, per favore. Ho un caffè. Che cosa vuoi?
npc.translation: Nice to meet you, Marco! One moment, please. I have a coffee. What do you want?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, you answered Leopold's question and asked for a coffee politely in Italian. We'll practise the other polite phrases a little later.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked for something and said please in Italian.
This time you didn't get Leopold's attention politely with an "excuse me" word, so Leopold will give you another chance to do that later.
You didn't tell Leopold that you don't understand this time, so that will come up again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Leopold is busy with something that matters only to Leopold. Get Leopold's attention politely, using Italian.
Leopold has just said something long, fast and apparently urgent. Tell Leopold that you do not understand, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Leopold pushes a piccola tazza across the tavolo with the air of a man closing a file. His timbro sits beside it, ancora unused, and the mattina is clear and chiara. Nearby, the silenzio remains molto unfilled.
npc.native: Ecco il caffè, Marco! Scusi, sono molto veloce. Scusi, va bene?
npc.translation: Here is the coffee, Marco! Sorry, I am very fast. Sorry, is that all right?

player: Scusi, Leopold! Grazie. Ma... non capisco.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely work! You politely got Leopold's attention, thanked him and told him you did not understand, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you got Leopold's attention politely with "Scusi".
Well done, "non capisco" is just right for saying you do not understand.

npc.narrative: Leopold lifts his timbro over the tazza, finds no motivo, and lowers it again, ancora una volta. The mattina is chiara, and the piazza has nothing to declare. He looks at you like a modulo that has been filled in correctly, which is disappointing.
npc.native: Bravo, Marco! Dici scusi, dici grazie e dici non capisco. Il caffè va bene?
npc.translation: Well done, Marco! You say sorry, you say thank you and you say I don't understand. Is the coffee all right?

player: Si, il caffè va bene. Grazie! Tu parli veloce, sì?

npc.narrative: You drink the caffè while Leopold watches the cup like a clerk watching a queue. His rubber stamp hovers over the saucer, finds nothing to approve, and retreats. The mattina is clear, and the tavolo is warm in the sun.
npc.native: Sì, Marco, parlo molto veloce! Ma per te parlo piano. Tu parli italiano?
npc.translation: Yes, Marco, I speak very fast! But for you I speak slowly. Do you speak Italian?

player: Un po'. Grazie per il caffè. Arrivederci!

npc.narrative: Leopold lifts his timbro over your goodbye, finds no modulo beneath it, and sets it down with some rimpianto. The cielo in the finestra is grigio, and the tazza on the bancone is still caldo. He leans closer, lentamente, which for him is a feat.
npc.native: Un po' va bene, Marco! Prego per il caffè. Vuoi un altro caffè?
npc.translation: A little is fine, Marco! You're welcome for the coffee. Do you want another coffee?
